result.title: Is It Still There? Place-Registered Verification Makes VLMs Reliable Scene-Change Detectors
result.summary: A robot that returns to a space must tell which objects were added, removed or moved since its last visit, while its trajectory, viewpoints and lighting differ between the two visits. We find that multi-image vision-language models (VLMs) fail at this task mainly because they cannot find the place where an object was. A VLM recognises what each frame shows but cannot check whether an object is still at its place in the other capture. It therefore reports objects that only one capture shows and misses most removed and moved objects. We propose STILL, which reformulates change detection as object verification at a registered place. 3D geometry registers the place of each change hypothesis in the other capture, and one VLM answers, from a scene view and a local place view, whether the object is still at that place, trained with supervision of the same form. Under the official SceneDiff protocol, STILL raises the main metric obj/sc AP from 24.0 to 37.8, and from 11.6 to 20.6 on the egocentric kitchen subset without any kitchen training data. It improves F1 by more than 21 points over a VLM fine-tuned on the same annotations and adds only about 11% to the runtime.

AI.brief_summary: 论文诊断多图 VLM 在场景变化检测中主要因无法定位物体原位置而失败，提出 STILL：用 3D 几何把变化候选的位置配准到另一次拍摄，再让 VLM 结合场景视图与局部位置视图判断物体是否仍在原处，并以同形式监督训练。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作直接涉及 VLM 如何在多视角间选取和核验视觉证据，与「LOOK 哪里」、物体级验证及何时停止判断相关；其位置配准与局部视图是否真正被模型使用，可供核查，但不涉及 latent 推理状态生成。
